jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Hardware
jobs.description:
ABOUT STANDARD BOTS

Standard Bots is building the world's most accessible robotics platform to bring advanced automation into manufacturing and beyond, with intuitive hardware and software that empower human productivity.  This role is onsite in either Glen Cove, NY or Boston, MA. 




OVERVIEW

Industrial hardware has been slow-moving and hard to iterate on for decades. We're trying to change that—bringing a consumer-grade pace of iteration and craft to a world that hasn't seen much of either. Most hardware products ship once and live with their decisions for years. Ours need to move fast, get into the field, get tested against reality, and improve—because a robot that doesn't hold up on a factory floor doesn't just frustrate a customer, it stops their production line.

We're looking for a Hardware PM who is a builder first. Someone who wants to own a product from a blank sheet of paper through to a customer relying on it every day. Someone who understands the market well enough to know what's worth building, and who treats every prototype as a question to be answered rather than an answer to be defended. Someone with product sense and taste who can tell the difference between "ships" and "good.”




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Own product discovery, strategy, and delivery for a hardware product area from 0-1—from market insight and concept through to a shipped, supportable product.

 - Build a sharp point of view on the market: who the customer is, what they're solving for today, where competitors fall short, and where the real opportunity is.

 - Drive iterative testing loops - prototype, test against real-world conditions, learn, and revise quickly.

 - Go deep on customer problems -talk to users, visit sites, understand how hardware actually gets used in the field.

 - Define what we're building and why, with clear specs and requirements that engineers can run with.

 - Work hands-on with mechanical, electrical, and firmware engineers to make trade-offs between cost, manufacturability, performance, and schedule.

 - Collaborate with design and engineering to de-risk assumptions early, before they're expensive to fix.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years in hardware product management, ideally with hands-on experience building robotics products.

 - Experience taking a hardware product from 0-1 - from early concept and market validation through to a released product.

 - You're comfortable running iterative test-and-learn cycles with physical prototypes, not just software.

 - You've built and shipped things you're proud of - not just managed process.

 - You think critically about customer and market problems and can break down ambiguity into structured decisions.

 - You have design and engineering sense and care about craft - you notice when something is off and it bothers you.

 - You communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Mechanical engineering degree (or related discipline), with real hands-on design or build experience.

 - Experience running structured tests on physical products - DOE, prototype validation, reliability or environmental testing.

 - Familiarity with CAD tools (SolidWorks, Fusion 360), DFM/DFA and manufacturing processes (injection molding, sheet metal, CNC), and electromechanical systems, motors, or controls - enough to read a drawing, sanity-check tolerances (GD&T), and make informed trade-offs with engineers.

 - Prior experience at a robotics, automation, or industrial equipment company, with a feel for how that market evaluates and buys products.

 - Startup experience owning a product end-to-end across both hardware and software, without staying confined to one discipline.




COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

The salary range for this role is $160,000 to $225,000, depending on experience. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (Immuware) - Remote, US
jobs.description:
Propelus® simplifies workforce compliance management across healthcare. Our innovative technology and strategic partnerships empower millions of professionals, their employers, and regulators to work together, creating a connected and efficient healthcare ecosystem.

As a trusted leader for over 20 years, Propelus has focused on bringing more good into the lives of the people and organizations serving healthcare. We deliver seamless compliance solutions to millions. We leverage market-leading technology and essential data to simplify complex operations, reduce risk, and champion a safer, healthier, and happier workforce.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

Immuware's customers, including Employee Health nurses; occupational health managers; and compliance professionals, work in one of the most requirement-heavy environments in healthcare IT. Regulations shift. Organizational structures change. New workflows emerge. Each of these changes often means hands-on work is needed inside their Immuware environment.

The Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) exists to meet that need. You are both technically driven and a proactive, friendly, and compelling person. 

You will be embedded in the post-sales customer experience, you are not an account management, not executing billable project work, and not break-fix support. 

You show up on customer calls, quickly understand the technical needs of a health-system nurse manager and what they are trying to accomplish, and provide the polished product quickly, ensuring a positive experience. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

As our Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) you will be the proactive technical resolution of customer problems end to end: 

From meticulously understanding the clients needs and proactively building those solutions, you ultimately serve as the bridge between customer needs and internal product and engineering teams. 

You're measured on customer outcomes, not on activity.
This role partners closely with our Customer Success Managers, who own the overall customer relationship, strategy, and commercial outcomes.



TECHNICAL SOLUTIONING & BUILDING

 - Lead regular (often weekly) technical working sessions with customers to address actively evolving needs driven by regulatory changes, organizational shifts, and workflow updates.

 - Identify, configure, script, and write code to solve customer needs: workflow setup, rule-building, field configuration, user and role management, reporting, data corrections, integrations, and small platform changes.

 - Translate complex Employee Health requirements (OSHA compliance, state-specific immunization mandates, system credentialing workflows, and the like) into solutions that actually work for our clients, in the Immuware platform.

 - Question their requirements and requests: Serving as the techncial expert, professionally challenge requests that don't serve the customer's real goal, and choose the simplest solution that solves the underlying problem to improve efficiency operationally. 

 - Thoroughly document your solution designs in Notion, while updating live items in Jira, to ensure they are clear, well-scoped bug reports and feature requests that are repeatable and transferable to enable engineering efficiency. 

 - Generalize your work: Turn one-off fixes into reusable templates, decision trees, or product improvements so the next customer benefits.

 - Triage net-new module or record-type additions that need a formal Letter of Work (LOW) and/or an ARR change (expansion) to CSMs and Professional Services.


CUSTOMER PARTNERSHIP

 - Serve as the technical counterpart to CSMs on customer calls: CSMs handle the relationship; you independently handle "how do we make it work."

 - Navigate internal client change: working alongside the CSMs, lead deeper, in-depth customer education beyond basic platform navigation, run workflow specific walkthroughs, and re-train as staff turnover and organizational change creates knowledge gaps.

 - Serve as the technical expert: build trusted-advisor relationships with power users and technical contacts at customer organizations. 
   
   - Proactively identify configuration gaps or risks before they turn into escalations, and execute solutions to maintain the strong client relationship

 - Detail Oriented: Stay aware of each assigned customer's various environment, history, and upcoming needs.
   
   - Confidently identify and navigate between "I can fix this," "this needs a support ticket," and "this needs a product change."


YOU'LL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Are energized by customer calls and like solving problems live, not async.

 - Can read a healthcare compliance requirement and immediately start thinking about how to model and build it in a SaaS platform.

 - Have a builder's mindset: you're systematic, you test your own work, you write code when it's the right tool, and you don't leave a solution half-done.

 - Can switch comfortably between explaining something to an IT admin, a head nurse, a customer executive, and your own engineering team.

 - Are naturally organized. You manage several customers with different environments and needs at once.

 - Get frustrated by workarounds and push internally for real solutions.


WE'D LIKE IT IF YOU HAD: 

 - 5+ years in a technical, customer-facing role (solutions engineer, implementation consultant, technical account manager, or forward deployed engineer) 
   
   - handling client resolutions, both live (virtually) and post meeting action items, and know how to navigate delays while staying calm under pressure and maintaining the clients trust.

 - 4-5 years navigating Azure, JavaScript, and Typescript with a strong background in SQL and Azure SQL database management.

 - 2-3+ experience operating in Notion and Jira

 - Proficiency in C#, and comfort reading a codebase, debugging, and writing scripts or small features, and track record of building on SaaS platforms, not just toggling settings: creating non-trivial workflows, rules, forms, reports, integrations, or role and permission structures.

 - Drive and ownership: You are comfortable and familiar with identifying the crux of large, enterprise customers' problems  and outline additional potential issues as well. Then you own the solution outcome, driving these problems to resolution on your own instead of handing them off.

 - Strong written and verbal communication: You're credible with a customer's executives and technical staff and with internal product and engineering teams, and comfortable leading technical working sessions with non-technical stakeholders.

 - You handle delays, bugs, and scope pushback while keeping the customer's trust.

 - Structured problem-solving: You have experience scoping an issue for large, enterprise clients, find the root cause, and propose a solution in a live setting and navigate how to implement these solutions to our smaller accounts.

 - Comfort working without a playbook: you'll hit novel problems regularly and need to adapt as policies and regulations change.

 - Written reporting experience: familiarity writing clear, well-scoped bug reports and feature requests that engineering teams can act on.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Experience in healthcare IT, Employee Health, or occupational health.

 - Familiarity with immunization tracking, credentialing workflows, or OSHA and state health reporting requirements.

 - Familiarity with APIs and integrations, plus comfort with SQL or scripting for data investigation and fixes.

 - Prior use of Immuware or similar platforms (Tyto Care, Equifax I-9, or Symplr)


WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT:

 - Not account ownership. CSMs own renewals, expansion, and the executive relationship. The FDE supports those relationships through technical excellence.

 - Not billable Professional Services. PS handles formal implementation projects with SOWs. The FDE handles ongoing, post-go-live technical needs as part of the customer's subscription.

 - Not the L1/L2 support queue. The support team owns routine bug triage. This FDE will do deeper scoping and fixes, ensuring a clean handoff. It does not replace the support workflow.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:

30 days: Support an active deal

Within the first month, you will have built context on the healthcare customers motion, platform capabilities, common implementation needs, and regulated data considerations. They are supporting an active customer engagement with guidance.

 

60 days: Lead a solo engagement

After two months, you are now independently leading a scoped customer sync, having built trust with customers technical teams, and delivering against customer requirements and timelines.

 

90 days: Own multiple, concurrent engagements

At three months in, you are now independently managing multiple healthcare customer engagements, contributing reusable playbooks and tooling, and surfacing product feedback that helps convert bespoke implementation patterns into scalable capabilities.

If your experience is close but doesn't fulfill all requirements, please apply. We're building the best team in healthcare and are focused on hiring individuals with unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences to support us in doing good, what’s human, and making a difference.

     - Where state or local leave laws provide additional protections, Propelus will comply with whichever regulation is more favorable to the employee.

Think of it as a bonus for the expenses and experiences you value most.

   - Carrot Fertility & Hormonal Support: Inclusive hormonal health, fertility, and family-building benefits with funds toward eligible care.

Benefits and Perks for ALL Propelus employees include but are not limited to:

A remote first company, global and distributed, with two office locations for those nearby who want a change of scenery.

Typical Interview Process:

We work remotely and communicate asynchronously, so writing is a key skill at Propelus. Please answer the application questions with your own thoughtful responses. Replies like "See resume" or N/A won't lead to an interview. Have some fun with it, we actually read these!

FIRST is part of the broader Encore family of companies. Encore is a global leader in event production and technology. Location: New York.  This is a hybrid role, must live in the NY tri state area and be able to go into office 2 days a week, subject to change to 5 days at any time.

Learn more at www.firstagency.com

What You Would Get To Do

jobs.title: Sr. Channel Sales Engineer
jobs.description:
JOB TITLE: SR. CHANNEL SALES ENGINEER

Location: Remote

Reports to: VP Global Sales Engineering




ABOUT WITNESSAI:

WitnessAI is the unified AI security and governance platform enterprises trust to govern and protect all AI activity. We provide complete, network-level visibility into every interaction including employees and autonomous agents, even in native apps where legacy tools are blind. Unlike security that relies on outdated keywords, our platform understands intent, enabling intelligent policies that stop novel threats like prompt injection while empowering productivity. WitnessAI transforms security from a bottleneck into the enabler of your AI strategy as the confidence layer for enterprise AI.


THE ROLE

As a Sr. Channel Sales Engineer, you are the technical lead for our partner ecosystem. You make resellers, distributors, MSSPs, and system integrators good at selling and deploying WitnessAI, and you join their deals when it counts.

This is a hands-on role. You will set the standard for how partners run demos and proofs of concept, and bring partner feedback back to Product and Sales. You work day to day with the Channel team, Sales Engineering, Product, and Marketing.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Enable partner technical teams. Train partner sales engineers and architects on the WitnessAI platform, the AI security market, and how to position us against legacy tools. Run onboarding, certification, and refresher sessions.

 - Support partner-led deals. Join partner calls and customer meetings to run demos, answer technical questions, and scope requirements. Step in on strategic deals, then coach partners to run the next one on their own.

 - Run proofs of concept. Define POC plans and success criteria with partners and customers. Guide the deployment, troubleshoot issues, and drive each POC to a clear decision.

 - Build partner technical assets. Create reference architectures, demo environments, deployment guides, battlecards, and talk tracks that partners can use without us in the room.

 - Partner on pipeline. Work with Channel Sales and Marketing on joint campaigns, workshops, and events. Help partners identify AI security use cases inside their existing customer base.

 - Answer security reviews and RFPs. Handle technical questionnaires, architecture reviews, and RFP responses that come through partners.

 - Bring back what you hear. Share partner and customer feedback with Product and Engineering. Flag integration gaps, competitive losses, and feature requests with specifics.

 - Represent WitnessAI. Present at partner events, conferences, and customer briefings.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 7+ years in pre-sales, sales engineering, or technical consulting, with at least 3 years supporting channel or partner sales.

 - A working understanding of network security, cloud infrastructure, identity, and data security. Familiarity with AI/ML or generative AI use cases is a strong plus.

 - A record of enabling partners to sell and deploy technical products, and of helping close six- and seven-figure deals through the channel.

 - Hands-on experience running demos and POCs end to end, including deployment and troubleshooting.

 - Experience working with resellers, distributors, MSSPs, or global system integrators.

 - Clear communication. You can explain a complex architecture to an engineer in the morning and a CISO in the afternoon.

 - Willingness to travel for partner and customer meetings and events.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Background at a cybersecurity vendor, especially in SASE, secure web gateway, CASB, DLP, or zero trust.

 - Experience building a partner enablement or certification program from scratch.

 - Existing relationships with security-focused VARs, MSSPs, or distributors.

 - Experience with partner portals and deal registration tools, plus CRM tools such as Salesforce.

 - Security or cloud certifications such as CISSP, AWS, Azure, or GCP.

 - Prior startup experience, where you built process because none existed.




WHY JOIN US

 - Build the technical foundation of our channel program in a new and fast-growing category.

 - Sell a product that solves one of the biggest problems in enterprise AI adoption.

 - Work directly with Sales, Product, and Engineering. Your feedback shapes the roadmap.

 - Competitive compensation and meaningful equity.

 - Backing from top investors and advisors in AI, cybersecurity, and enterprise software.




BENEFITS:

 - Competitive salary and equity

 - Health, dental, and vision insurance

 - 401(k) plan

 - Opportunities for professional development and growth

 - Generous vacation policy




SALARY RANGE:

$260,000 - $295,000 OTE (The exact salary will be determined based on the selected candidate's location, qualifications, experience, and relevant skills.)

jobs.title: Heavy Diesel Equipment Mechanics
jobs.description:
Copper River Technologies is seeking experienced Journeyman Heavy Diesel Equipment Mechanics to support maintenance operations for NAVFAC in Crane, Indiana. This position supports the Navy’s 3M Maintenance Program and is responsible for independently performing preventative and corrective maintenance on a wide range of heavy-duty vehicles, construction equipment, generators, and support systems in a mission-driven environment.

The ideal candidate will possess strong troubleshooting and repair experience involving diesel engines, hydraulics, electrical systems, and heavy construction equipment while maintaining strict adherence to safety and quality standards.

Responsibilities (include but are not limited to):

• Perform preventative and corrective maintenance on heavy and light vehicles and equipment in accordance with Navy 3M Maintenance Program requirements

• Diagnose and repair diesel engines, hydraulic systems, electrical systems, and mechanical components

• Conduct routine maintenance services including oil changes, fluid replacements, brake repairs, tire repair/replacement, and electrical troubleshooting

• Inspect, test, and repair heavy tracked and wheeled construction equipment

• Complete and maintain accurate maintenance documentation and 3M work reports

• Research and identify required repair parts and provide ordering information to Government personnel

• Ensure all repairs meet quality standards with minimal rework required

• Follow all safety, environmental, lockout/tagout, and PPE requirements

• Support maintenance scheduling, technical evaluations, and project coordination activities

• Coordinate effectively with Government personnel, project managers, and team members

• Maintain tools, equipment, and workspaces in a clean and safe condition

• Perform work both indoors and outdoors in varying environmental conditions

• Mechanics may support maintenance and repair of equipment including: HMMWVs and MTVRs Bulldozers, graders, and front-end loaders KALMAR Rough Terrain Cargo Handlers (RTCH) Forklifts Buses, vans, pickups, and SUVs Generators and light plants Other gasoline- and diesel-powered equipment

Essential Job Qualifications and Requirements:

• Clearance: Ability to obtain/maintain required access credentials as needed

• Education and Certifications: Ability to successfully complete Navy 3M Maintenance Program training Valid driver’s license required

• Required Experience: Journeyman-level experience as a Heavy Diesel or Heavy Equipment Mechanic Demonstrated experience troubleshooting and repairing diesel engines, hydraulics, electrical systems, and gasoline-powered equipment Experience working on heavy tracked and wheeled construction equipment

• Required Skill and Competencies Ability to work independently with minimal supervision Familiarity with Microsoft Office Suite and basic computer systems Strong understanding of safety and environmental compliance procedures Working knowledge of: Diesel and gasoline internal combustion engines Hydraulics Mechanical systems Electrical systems Brakes and steering systems Generators and electrical equipment Material-handling and construction equipment

• Work Environment Work is primarily performed indoors in maintenance bays, with occasional outdoor work required Exposure to varying weather conditions and loud equipment environments Shared workspace environment with Government personnel Safety-sensitive environment requiring strict adherence to PPE and safety protocols

• Physical Requirements Ability to lift, carry, and maneuver heavy equipment components Ability to stand, kneel, bend, and work in confined spaces for extended periods Ability to work around loud equipment and machinery

Owned by the Native Village of Eyak (NVE), a federally recognized Alaska Native Tribe, the Copper River Family of Companies are a collection of entities that deliver a complementary set of solutions and services to support the diverse missions and requirements of our clients. Proud participants of the Small Business Administration’s (SBA) 8(a) Business Development Program since 2006, our companies consist of both current and graduation SBA 8(a) entities. It is our collective purpose to support the Tribe and diversify the NVE’s ability to facilitate economic advancement.

The income generated from our companies helps the Native Village of Eyak fund health and social services, economic development, natural resource/environmental education, jobs, job training, and other benefits to the NVE in a manner that is consistent with Alaskan Native cultural values and traditions.

Copper River’s Culture

The Copper River Family of Companies has a positive, supportive, and thriving culture. At the foundation of our culture is a focus on collaboration. No matter your role or which operating company you work for, we are ONE TEAM working toward the same goals for our customers and for our collective owner- The Native Village of Eyak. How we treat each other is just as important as the work we deliver.

jobs.title: Sr. 401(k) Onboarding Associate
jobs.description:
About Betterment

Betterment is a leading, technology-driven financial services company that offers investing, savings and retirement solutions for retail investors and investment advisors as well as financial wellness solutions, including a 401(k) for small and medium-sized businesses. Our team is passionate about our mission, to empower people to build wealth with confidence and ease.  We’re headquartered in NYC and offer hybrid NY-based positions (four days/ week in-office, with no required office days during the summer and winter holidays).

About the role

The Senior 401(k) Onboarding Associate's main focus is to help guide Betterment at Work’s clients through a pleasant and efficient onboarding experience.

In this role, the Onboarding Associate will contribute to a cross functional work environment by facilitating a seamless hand off from the sales team and successfully driving a client through to their first payroll launch on the Betterment platform. The Onboarding Associate will liaise with the 401(k) compliance team to help design and implement a client’s 401(k) plan design. This role reports into the Sr. Manager of 401(k) Onboarding.

This is a salaried, exempt role that is remote eligible, except for the New York City metro area, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Seattle, Boston, Washington, D.C., & Orange County, CA. jobs.title: Engineer
jobs.description:
This is a U.S. based position. All of the programs we support require U.S. citizenship to be eligible for employment. All work must be conducted within the continental U.S.

Who we are:

Raft (https://TeamRaft.com) is a customer-obsessed non-traditional defense tech company dedicated to empowering U.S. military and government agencies with cutting-edge AI/ML and data solutions. We are a leader in autonomous data fusion and Agentic AI, with a purposeful focus on Distributed Data Systems, Platforms at Scale, and Complex Application Development. With headquarters in McLean, VA, our range of clients includes innovative federal and public agencies leveraging design thinking, cutting-edge tech stack, and cloud-native ecosystem. We build digital solutions that impact the lives of millions of Americans.

About the role:

Raft builds mission-critical data, AI, and operational platforms that support time-sensitive decisions across multiple classification levels and deployment environments. Our systems move from cloud-hosted development environments into classified, on-premises, and edge deployments where reliability, security, and repeatability matter.

As an DevOps Engineer, you will help secure, deploy, and operate the platforms behind [R]DP, [R]AP, [R]AIMS, and Raft’s MLOps workflows. This is not a narrow infrastructure role. You will learn how the software works, how data moves through the platform, how Kubernetes workloads behave in production, and how security controls become part of everyday delivery rather than an after-the-fact checklist.

What makes this role different is the breadth of what you’ll be exposed to. CI/CD, GitOps, Kubernetes, Helm charts, observability, secure configuration, data pipelines, ML serving, and customer deployments all show up in the same workstream. You will work alongside experienced platform, software, data, and security engineers while taking ownership of well-scoped work. The right person is curious, disciplined, willing to troubleshoot deeply, and ready to grow into broader platform ownership over time.

What You’ll Do

• Implement, maintain, and troubleshoot Kubernetes-based platform infrastructure under the guidance of senior engineers

• Build and maintain CI/CD and GitOps workflows using tools such as GitLab CI, Argo CD, Flux, Helm, and repository-managed deployment configuration

• Support secure software delivery practices including container hardening, vulnerability scanning, image provenance checks, secrets hygiene, and policy-driven deployment gates

• Help operate cloud, on-premises, and disconnected deployments across AWS, Azure, data center, and tactical environments

• Deploy and debug services, Helm charts, service mesh configuration, Kubernetes networking, storage, and runtime behavior

• Support observability across Prometheus, Grafana, Fluent Bit, Loki, Kibana, OpenTelemetry, or similar tooling so issues can be detected and resolved quickly

• Work with software and data engineers to understand service dependencies, data flows, and operational failure modes

• Support data and MLOps workloads that may include Kafka, Flink, Pinot, KServe, Kubeflow, Ray, GPU-enabled workloads, and model-serving workflows

• Write maintainable automation and small tools in Go, Java, Python, Bash, or similar languages to reduce manual effort and improve repeatability

• Contribute to compliance-driven delivery practices aligned with RMF, STIGs, NIST 800-53, IL4/IL5/IL6, and customer-specific security requirements

• Document operational procedures, deployment notes, troubleshooting steps, and lessons learned in a way other engineers can reuse

What we are looking for:

• 5 years of hands-on experience in DevSecOps, DevOps, platform engineering, cloud infrastructure, systems administration, cybersecurity engineering, or a closely related role

• Working familiarity with Linux, containers, Docker, and Kubernetes concepts, including pods, services, deployments, config maps, secrets, ingress, and basic troubleshooting

• Experience building, running, or supporting CI/CD pipelines; exposure to GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Argo CD, Flux, or similar tools

• Exposure to Infrastructure as Code or configuration management with Terraform, Ansible, Helm, Kustomize, or similar tooling

• Understanding of foundational security practices such as least privilege, vulnerability management, container image scanning, secrets handling, secure configuration, and auditability

• Ability to read application logs, inspect runtime configuration, use command-line tooling, and follow evidence to root cause

• Basic scripting or programming ability in Go, Java, Python, Bash, or a comparable language

• Interest in data platforms, streaming systems, MLOps, and operational AI/ML workloads; prior exposure to Kafka, Flink, KServe, Kubeflow, or Ray is a plus

• Strong written communication and willingness to document work clearly for teammates, customers, and future operators

• Active Secret clearance required; must be eligible for and willing to obtain a Top Secret/SCI clearance

• Ability to obtain Security+ certification within the first 90 days of employment

• Ability to travel up to 30%

Highly preferred:

• Hands-on experience deploying applications with Helm or Kustomize in a Kubernetes environment

• Exposure to GitOps workflows and continuous delivery across multiple environments

• Familiarity with AWS or Azure fundamentals including IAM, networking, storage, compute, and managed Kubernetes services

• Exposure to service mesh technologies such as Istio, including mTLS, traffic routing, and observability concepts

• Familiarity with security and compliance frameworks used in government delivery, including RMF, STIGs, FedRAMP, NIST 800-53, and IL4/IL5/IL6 controls

• Experience supporting air-gapped, disconnected, classified, or resource-constrained deployments

• Exposure to SBOMs, SCA, SAST, DAST, container scanning, admission control, OPA/Gatekeeper, Kyverno, Sigstore, or similar supply chain security tooling

• Existing TS/SCI clearance strongly preferred

What Success Looks Like

• You reliably execute assigned deployment, automation, observability, and security tasks with clear communication and good follow-through

• You can explain what changed, why it changed, how it was verified, and what risk remains

• You grow quickly from following runbooks to improving them, then to owning small platform improvements end to end

• Senior engineers trust you with well-defined operational work because you investigate carefully and escalate the right issues early

• Security and compliance practices show up in your daily work: pipelines, manifests, secrets, images, documentation, and operational handoffs are kept clean

Clearance Requirements:

• Active Secret Clearance to start required; TS eligibility required

Salary Range: $140,000.00 - $180,000.00

Work Type:

• Hybrid in Colorado Springs, with up to 30% travel

What we will offer you:

• Highly competitive salary

• Fully covered healthcare, dental, and vision coverage

• 401(k) and company match

• Take as you need PTO + 11 paid holidays

• Education & training benefits

• Generous Referral Bonuses

• And More!

Our Vision Statement:

We bridge the gap between humans and data through radical transparency and our obsession with the mission.

Our Customer Obsession:

We will approach every deliverable like it's a product. We will adopt a customer-obsessed mentality. As we grow, and our footprint becomes larger, teams and employees will treat each other not only as teammates but customers. We must live the customer-obsessed mindset, always. This will help us scale and it will translate to the interactions that our Rafters have with their clients and other product teams that they integrate with. Our culture will enable our success and set us apart from other companies.

How do we get there?

Public-sector modernization is critical for us to live in a better world. We, at Raft, want to innovate and solve complex problems. And, if we are successful, our generation and the ones that follow us will live in a delightful, efficient, and accessible world where out-of-box thinking, and collaboration is a norm.

Raft’s core philosophy is Ubuntu: I Am, Because We are. We support our “nadi” by elevating the other Rafters. We work as a hyper collaborative team where each team member brings a unique perspective, adding value that did not exist before. People make Raft special. We celebrate each other and our cognitive and cultural diversity. We are devoted to our practice of innovation and collaboration.

We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

jobs.title: Registered Behavior Technician
jobs.description:
We are looking for enthusiastic individuals to join our team as Behavior Technicians. As a Behavior Technician, you will have the opportunity to make a real difference in the lives of children with autism.

In this role, you will work one-on-one with children, implementing individualized behavior intervention plans under the guidance of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA). You will use evidence-based techniques to teach communication, social, and daily living skills while reducing interfering behaviors.

We are looking for candidates who are passionate about helping children with autism reach their full potential. You will need to be patient, compassionate, and able to work well in a team environment. We will provide comprehensive training so that you are equipped and empowered to help each child, even if you don’t currently have experience. Children can be unpredictable and potentially confrontational, so this role is not for the weak of spirit, mind, or body. Part of the joy of working with kids is exercise! Our clients move, so you need to be comfortable standing, walking, sitting, grasping, reaching, bending, kneeling, crouching, squatting, lifting, and at times carrying children or objects that weigh up to 50 pounds.

At the end of each day, you will go home knowing that you have made a meaningful impact on the life of a child and their family. Join us and become a part of a dedicated team that is changing lives for the better. Apply now to start your journey as a Behavior Technician with us!

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Lead, Data Centers - Remote (U.S.)
jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking a Senior Mechanical Engineer with experience on Hyperscale Data Center projects to act as Data Center Mechanical Engineer Lead. The job incumbent will be responsible for designing and overseeing the construction of mechanical systems for hyperscale data centers, including HVAC, piping and fire suppression systems.  This position is based in Arlington, VA, however, is open to other AECOM office locations and remote work under certain circumstances.

The Mechanical Engineer will play a critical role in ensuring the reliability, efficiency, and safety of our data center infrastructure. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in mechanical engineering and experience working with high-density data centers.

This position offers the flexibility of a remote work schedule and can be based from a variety of locations in the US where AECOM has an office.

Although the position is primarily remote periodic travel may be required for client meetings, key project milestones, onsite collaboration sessions, or other business‑critical activities. Travel is expected to be occasional and scheduled in advance

AECOM is a leader in the global data center consulting industry with robust teams in the Americas, Europe, Africa, Asia, and Australia.  In this role, you will have the opportunity to work with our teams around the world on high-profile, fast-paced data center projects for global clients.  This is a hands-on, client-facing role with an opportunity for upward career mobility.

JOB SUMMARY:

• Act as the primary point of contact for clients, responding to their inquiries and concerns in a timely and professional manner
• Develop and maintain strong relationships with clients, regularly communicating with them to understand their needs and expectations
• Coordinating with multiple disciplines and acting as lead mechanical engineer to ensure that projects are delivered within budget and on schedule while managing the mechanical team including HVAC, fire protection, plumbing
• Develop detailed specifications for mechanical equipment, including pumps, fans, and air handling units.
• Writing reports for internal and external purposes based on findings
• Ensures discipline plans that are created to meet overall project team requirements for project scope and schedule
• Stays current on codes and technologies appropriate to the mechanical, plumbing and fire protection systems related to hyperscale data centers
• Analyze and evaluate mechanical system performance, identifying areas for improvement and making recommendations for upgrades
• Provide technical support during the construction phase, responding to RFIs and addressing any issues that arise
• Attend job site visits, project meetings, and commissioning activities as needed
• Ensure compliance with industry standards, codes, and regulations
• Evaluate and recommend new technologies and equipment to enhance system performance and reduce operational costs
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including electrical and mechanical engineers, to ensure seamless integration of the chiller systems with other data center infrastructure
• Analyze energy usage, identifying opportunities for optimization and cost savings.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering plus ten (10) years of relevant experience in mechanical design and/or mechanical engineering, with a focus on data center infrastructure, or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
• Professional Engineer License (P.E.) is required

Preferred Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering plus twelve (12) years of relevant experience in mechanical design and/or mechanical engineering, with a focus on data center infrastructure, or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
• Extensive experience in mechanical engineering for data centers or other critical facilities.
• Strong knowledge of HVAC, piping, and fire suppression systems design and construction.
• Strong leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills
• Ability to build and maintain strong relationships with clients
• Ability to think creatively and identify opportunities to enhance the client experience.
• Experience working with computer-aided design (CAD) and building information modeling (BIM) software
• Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills
• Experience with data center design and construction, including design criteria and industry standards

jobs.title: Senior Reverse Engineering/Vulnerability Research Engineer
jobs.description:
Clarity Innovations is a trusted national security partner, dedicated to safeguarding our nation’s interests and delivering innovative solutions that empower the Intelligence Community (IC) and Department of Defense (DoD) to transform data into actionable intelligence, ensuring mission success in an evolving world.

Our mission-first software and data engineering platform modernizes data operations, utilizing advanced workflows, CI/CD, and secure DevSecOps practices. We focus on challenges in Information Warfare, Cyber Operations, Operational Security, and Data Structuring, enabling end-to-end solutions that drive operational impact.

We are committed to delivering cutting-edge tools and capabilities that address the most complex national security challenges, empowering our partners to stay ahead of emerging threats and ensuring the success of their critical missions. At Clarity, we are people-focused and set on being a destination employer for top talent, offering an environment where innovation thrives, careers grow, and individuals are valued. Join us as we continue to lead innovation and tackle the most pressing challenges in national security.

Principal Security Researcher

Clarity Innovations
Discipline: Reverse Engineering / Vulnerability Research
Location: Hybrid
Clearance: TS/SCI

Company Overview

Clarity Innovations equips customers with the technology, expertise, and support needed to conduct successful cyber operations. We bring together talented engineers, researchers, and operators to solve some of the U.S. Government’s most challenging technical problems. Our teams combine technical excellence, creativity, and collaboration to deliver capabilities that advance customer missions.

Role

Clarity Innovations is seeking a Principal Security Researcher to lead complex vulnerability research and reverse engineering efforts. In this role, you will investigate how systems function, identify security weaknesses, and develop capabilities that demonstrate their impact within customer-authorized research activities.

You will provide technical leadership throughout the research lifecycle—from initial exploration and research planning through vulnerability discovery, exploitation, documentation, and delivery. Working alongside experienced security researchers, you will apply advanced static and dynamic analysis techniques across diverse architectures and operating environments.

The ideal candidate brings deep technical expertise, sound research judgment, the ability to guide teams through ambiguous problems, and troubleshoot basic networking issues. Success requires clear communication with technical and non-technical stakeholders, a collaborative approach, and a commitment to developing fellow researchers.

Responsibilities

• Lead vulnerability research and reverse engineering efforts aligned with customer objectives.

• Define research strategies, assess technical feasibility, and guide teams through project planning, kickoff, execution, and delivery.

• Perform advanced static and dynamic analysis using disassemblers, debuggers, emulators, tracers, and fuzzers.

• Identify vulnerabilities, conduct root-cause analysis, and document reproducible findings.

• Develop reliable proof-of-concept exploits and operational exploit capabilities for authorized customer requirements.

• Evaluate and bypass modern exploit mitigations and security mechanisms as part of authorized research.

• Build tooling, automation, and research infrastructure that improve vulnerability discovery, analysis, and reproducibility.

• Communicate research progress, technical risks, findings, and recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Share research findings internally and externally when authorized and appropriate.

• Mentor security researchers, review technical work, and promote rigorous research and documentation practices.

• Lead small to medium-sized research teams, maintaining technical quality and alignment with project objectives.

Minimum Qualifications

• Ability to obtain and maintain a TS/SCI security clearance; U.S. citizenship is required.

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline. Four years of hands-on experience in software engineering or a comparable full-time technical role may substitute for the degree.

• Demonstrated experience conducting vulnerability research and reverse engineering, including independently driving complex technical investigations.

• Experience providing technical leadership and mentoring engineers or security researchers.

• Experience using Ghidra, Binary Ninja, IDA, or comparable reverse engineering and disassembly tools.

• Strong knowledge of Linux internals and fundamentals, including sockets, file descriptors, networking, iptables, file systems, and kernel behavior.

• Ability to read and write C and work with assembly languages for architectures such as ARM, MIPS, and x86-64.

• Strong programming fundamentals, including networking, data structures, and data models.

• Understanding of exploitation techniques, including arbitrary read/write primitives, shellcode development, return-oriented programming, and jump-oriented programming.

• Experience participating in capture-the-flag competitions, hackathons, or other cybersecurity competitions.

• Ability to clearly communicate complex technical concepts and produce actionable research documentation.

Preferred Qualifications

• Active Top Secret security clearance.

• Experience reverse engineering operating systems and kernels.

• Experience with fuzzing tools such as AFL++ or libFuzzer.

• Knowledge of security controls and exploit mitigations, including SELinux, seccomp, ASLR, and control-flow integrity.

• Advanced dynamic analysis experience using GDB, gdbserver, or comparable tools.

• Familiarity with processor toolchains and the Android Native Development Kit.

• Experience using QEMU or Unicorn to emulate code in non-native environments.

• Demonstrated experience discovering previously unknown vulnerabilities, including zero-days.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Clarity Innovations is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

Salary Range: $106,000 - $277,000

Pay Range

The posted pay range reflects the anticipated base salary range for this position and is provided to give candidates a general understanding of the compensation opportunity. The actual salary offered will be determined based on the requirements of the position and a variety of job-related factors, which may include geographic location, applicable Federal Government contract labor categories and wage rates, relevant experience, skills and competencies, education, certifications, and the scope and responsibilities of the role.

Because this position may be performed in multiple locations and may be subject to different contract requirements, the salary ultimately offered may vary based on the applicable location and contract. The posted range is not a guarantee of a specific starting salary or an indication that an offer will be made at any particular point within the range.

Total Rewards

In addition to competitive base pay, Clarity provides a Total Rewards package designed to attract and retain exceptional professionals committed to excellence. Our benefits reflect the value we place on skilled individuals who drive our impact in critical digital missions.

At Clarity, a career means joining a high-performing team advancing vital work in the digital landscape. We encourage you to consider the total value of joining us—competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and resources that support your growth and impact.

Our Total Rewards package includes performance-based bonuses, extensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) plan with company match, substantial paid time off and holidays, flexible work arrangements where possible, and a range of income protection benefits. We are committed to supporting your well-being, professional growth, and ability to contribute to essential digital missions.

We are an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

jobs.title: Air Operations Planner
jobs.description:
This is a U.S. based position. All of the programs we support require U.S. citizenship to be eligible for employment. All work must be conducted within the continental U.S.

Who we are:

Raft (https://TeamRaft.com) is a customer-obsessed non-traditional defense tech company dedicated to empowering U.S. military and government agencies with cutting-edge AI/ML and data solutions. We are a leader in autonomous data fusion and Agentic AI, with a purposeful focus on Distributed Data Systems, Platforms at Scale, and Complex Application Development. With headquarters in McLean, VA, our range of clients includes innovative federal and public agencies leveraging design thinking, cutting-edge tech stack, and cloud-native ecosystem. We build digital solutions that impact the lives of millions of Americans.

We’re looking for an experienced Air Operations Planner (AOP) to support our growing efforts and join our passionate team of high-impact problem solvers. This is a unique opportunity to help build and shape a game-changing organization where we put our customers and people first.

About the role:

Raft is providing direct support to the Air Operations Center (AOC) Strategy Division. This position is responsible for leading long-range and near-term planning, guidance, and operational assessment of Joint Air Operations. Your involvement in this role will encompass hands-on collaboration with a team of accomplished individuals, collectively striving towards excellence.

• Provide detailed Mission Analysis reflecting customer requirements throughout the Joint Operation Planning Process.

• Analyze foreign military air, space and cyberspace operations to assess and document threats to infrastructure, digital equipment and intellectual technologies.

jobs.title: MRO Buyer
jobs.description:
Overview of the Role

The MRO Buyer ensures the plant has the maintenance parts, supplies, and services needed to support safe, reliable operations. This role combines spare-parts and storeroom coordination with MRO purchasing, supplier follow-up, and inventory control. The successful candidate will have hands-on experience with SAP S/4HANA, including relevant purchasing and inventory transactions, and will work closely with Maintenance, Production, Warehouse, Finance, Procurement, and suppliers.

What We Are Looking For!

• Maintain accurate inventory records for maintenance spare parts, consumables, and MRO supplies.
• Monitor usage, inventory levels, lead times, and part criticality; recommend reorder points, minimum and maximum quantities, and stocking strategies.
• Coordinate cycle counts and physical inventories, investigate discrepancies, and help maintain inventory accuracy.
• Ensure parts are identified, labeled, stored, and preserved for safe and efficient retrieval.
• Review requests for new stock items, identify existing or interchangeable parts where appropriate, and support clear item descriptions and specifications.
• Track stockouts, emergency issues, slow-moving items, and obsolete inventory; communicate risks and recommend corrective actions.
• Coordinate the issue of parts to authorized employees and ensure inventory transactions are recorded promptly and accurately.
• Source and purchase maintenance parts, tools, supplies, and services in accordance with company purchasing procedures and approval limits.
• Convert approved requisitions into purchase orders, confirming specifications, quantities, pricing, delivery requirements, and account coding.
• Obtain and compare supplier quotations and recommend options based on total cost, quality, availability, and delivery.
• Coordinate with suppliers on order confirmations, lead times, backorders, substitutions, returns, warranties, and invoice or delivery discrepancies.
• Expedite critical orders and communicate order status and supply risks to Maintenance and Production.
• Support supplier onboarding, performance reviews, and sourcing initiatives with Procurement and other authorized teams.
• Maintain purchasing documentation and follow applicable approval, recordkeeping, and internal-control requirements.
• Support planned maintenance and shutdown preparation by coordinating material availability and identifying long-lead or critical items.
• Participate in reviews of equipment bills of materials, spare-parts lists, and maintenance-related inventory data.
• Use SAP S/4HANA and designated experience with CMMS – Fiix preferred, ERP, inventory, and purchasing systems to support purchasing and inventory accuracy.
• Identify opportunities to improve storeroom processes, purchasing workflows, inventory performance, and supplier service.
• Follow site safety, environmental, quality, security, and housekeeping requirements; promptly report hazards, incidents, and compliance concerns.
• Perform other related duties as assigned.

What You Will Bring!

• Experience in industrial purchasing, MRO procurement, maintenance storeroom operations, inventory control, or a related manufacturing function. Equivalent combinations of education and experience may be considered.
• Hands-on experience with SAP S/4HANA purchasing and inventory transactions.
• College degree, technical coursework, or relevant training in supply chain, procurement, business, maintenance, or inventory management preferred.
• Proficiency with spreadsheets and business systems, with the ability to use ERP, CMMS, inventory, and purchasing software.
• Strong attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate inventory and purchasing records.
• Effective communication, organization, and follow-through skills.
• Ability to prioritize requests and manage multiple open orders and deadlines in a manufacturing environment.

jobs.description:
The position is based in Lake County within Global R&D Capital Planning and reports to the Director, Global R&D Capital Planning. The incumbent will support the global Request for Capital Expenditure (RCE) lifecycle across R&D and serve as a key business partner to stakeholders across Business, Engineering, Finance, EHS and other relevant functions.

The role coordinates complex capital investment requests from early development through management approval. The incumbent will also help design, deploy, execute, and continuously improve a globally aligned RCE operating model while providing analytical and coordination support for Annual Plan and Long-Range Planning activities.

This role requires a collaborative, process-oriented individual who can quickly learn the RCE process, connect stakeholders across sites and functions, drive execution in a matrix environment, and build scalable team capability to deliver the work effectively.

Major Responsibilities:

RCE Lifecycle Leadership

• Serve as a primary business partner for assigned R&D organizations throughout the RCE lifecycle.
• Coordinate the development, review, submission, governance, approval, and closeout of capital investment requests.
• Lead complex and strategically significant RCEs through senior executive governance, including Board and CEO approval when required.
• Ensure submissions are decision-ready and meet business, engineering, financial, EHS, compliance, and governance requirements.

Stakeholder Coordination and Business Partnership

• Build relationships across US sites connecting Engineering, Facilities, Finance, Business Operations, EHS, and IT stakeholders.
• Facilitate alignment, clarify ownership, resolve issues, coordinate escalations, and translate technical, financial, and business inputs into clear investment proposals and recommendations.
• Prepare clear, decision-ready proposal content that connects project scope, business rationale, financial assumptions, risks, and governance requirements.

Contractor and Workload Coordination

• Develop, coordinate, and provide day-to-day guidance to external RCE-writing resources supporting a high volume of requests.
• Prioritize workload, balance capacity, set quality expectations, and coach contractors toward consistent delivery.
• Capture lessons learned from supported RCEs and translate recurring insights into practical improvements to templates, guidance, and ways of working.

Qualifications:

Education and Experience

• Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, IT, Project Management, Engineering, Life Sciences, or a related discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
• 5+ years of relevant experience, with demonstrated progression in engineering, capital projects, facilities, business operations, finance, program management, or a related field.
• This role is intended as a development opportunity for a high-performing employee who wants to build deep expertise in R&D capital governance and grow into a recognized end-to-end RCE lifecycle partner.
• Demonstrated success coordinating complex, cross-functional work in a matrix organization.
• Experience with capital investments, project approvals, portfolio governance, or executive decision processes preferred.

Skills and Competencies

• Ability to rapidly develop expertise in R&D capital governance and the end-to-end RCE lifecycle.
• Excellent stakeholder management, influencing, facilitation, and executive communication skills.
• Strong process thinking, analytical judgment, problem-solving, and disciplined execution.
• Ability to lead through influence, manage competing priorities, and work effectively across sites, functions, and cultures.
• Experience developing people or coordinating contractors, with a strong focus on quality and accountability.
• Practical experience using AI-enabled tools to improve productivity, with curiosity and comfort applying AI in business workflows without requiring a technical IT background.

jobs.title: Patient Care Tech-Cardiac Pulmonary Medicine 11W Full-time Nights
jobs.description:
The Patient Care Technician reflects the mission, vision, and values of Northwestern Memorial, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Patient Care Technician’s primary function is to assist and support the Professional Registered Nurse in all aspects of direct and indirect patient care activities.  The Patient Care Technician functions as a member of the unit staff under the direction and supervision of the professional Registered Nurse.

Responsibilities:

• Direct Patient Care Activities Assists with admission, transfer, and discharge process.Takes and records temperature, pulse, respirations, weight for adults and/or neonates, height, and blood pressure.Measures and records intake and output including output from drains.Applies cardiac monitor/oximetry.Obtains EKG.Adheres to the infant security protocol (accurate assessment of band placement).Performs normal newborn hearing screening.Obtains capillary blood glucose for adults and/or neonates.Performs phlebotomy.Applies Fetal Monitor equipment on pregnant patients.Discontinues heplocks and foley catheters. Administers enemas.Collects specimens (urine, stool, blood and sputum) on adults and/or neonates. Makes rounds of patients and anticipates their needs and observes newborns in the nursery.Responds to patient call lights in a timely manner, especially emergency lights.Distributes fresh drinking water and nourishments to patients. Prepares patients for meals; assists or feeds patients as necessary. Feeds normal newborns as assigned.Provides morning care, bed baths and evening care according to established Nursing Care Procedures. Provides peri-care to appropriate patients.Provides newborn care to the infant including bath, dressing, obtaining foot prints, assistance with feeding (bottle and breast), glucose checks.Makes occupied and unoccupied beds.Ambulates patients and instructs on walker, cane and crutch walking as appropriate for assigned unit. Assists with pre-and post-operative care; positions patients as ordered; applies special equipment for safety; lifts and turns patients with proper and safe body mechanics and available resources.Applies comfort and safety measures (side rails and call lights). Sets up oxygen and suction equipment and other respiratory equipment for adults and/or neonates.Applies dressings to Stage I and Stage II skin breakdown. Prepares patient room for MD or RN assessment, evaluation, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. Assists with procedures in the normal newborn nursery as directed.Transports patients, equipment and/or supplies during urgent and emergent situations and to front door on discharge.Responds to emergency situations, secures assistance and initiates basic life support.Reports observations and documents appropriately. Promptly notifies RN of any change in patient condition.Performs post-mortem care and transports bodies to the morgue when necessary.Assumes responsibility for the care of patient’s prosthetic devices, hearing aides, dentures, eye glasses, etc.Follows established policies, procedures and standards of care in all areas of practice.

• Indirect Patient CareMaintains a safe and clean environment. Duties may include: maintaining temperature logs on, defrosting, and cleaning refrigerator, straightening linen, cleaning utility rooms, cleaning IV poles, cleaning scale, cleaning and returning equipment to SPD, replacing and disposing of soiled linen bags.Performs duties delegated by the RN to facilitate patient care and the efficient operations of the assigned patient care unit.Collects and inventories patient belongings on admission, transfer and discharge.Completes charges using appropriate documentation.Orders supplies on-line or appropriate requisitions and stocks in appropriate location.Obtains necessary equipment and supplies to facilitate patient care.Assures room readiness for incoming patients.Checks designated equipment for proper functioning.Counts instruments and sterile trays sent and received from SEP as appropriate for assigned unit.Stocks and removes linen from patient rooms.Sets up and breaks down delivery table.Participates in staff meetings.Demonstrates cost effective approach to patient care in terms of equipment, supplies and other resource use.Participates in quality improvement activities.Participates in daily/weekly/monthly QC’s.Participates in orientation of new staff.Performs related duties as assigned.Uses established communication channels to resolve work related problems.Understands and consistently demonstrates principles of “Patient’s First” philosophy.Carries out assigned tasks and activities on a shift basis, as delegated by the RN.Assumes responsibility for meeting mandatory requirements.

Required:

• CNA Certification or currently enrolled in School of Nursing who has successfully completed basic clinical rotations.
• CPR recognition by the American Heart Association (BLS for Healthcare Providers).
• Minimum of 90% correct on annual mandatory Health and Safety Training quizzes.
• Unit based recognition for Capillary Blood Glucose Monitoring.
• High school diploma required. One year of college or nursing education or equivalent experience preferred.
• Previous experience in a health care setting preferred with a demonstrated ability to relate to patients, family, nursing and medical staff.

Preferred:

• Associates or Bachelor’s degree.

Northwestern Medicine is an equal opportunity employer (disability, VETS) and does not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of age, sex, race, color, religion, national origin, gender identity, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation or any other protected status.

jobs.title: Director, Communications and Voice
jobs.description:
Director, Communications and Voice

The Role

Help shape Plexus's voice and turn business priorities into communications that inspire action.

We are looking for a collaborative communications leader and exceptional writer to build a unified strategy that connects our Ambassadors, customers, employees, and the public. As the guardian of the Plexus voice, you will define how our brand sounds and ensure our messaging builds trust, strengthens engagement, and supports growth.

As Plexus expands into more channels, you will help evolve how we reach and connect with our audiences. Working closely with Sales, Marketing, and international teams, you will lead communications for product launches, promotions, incentives, events, and company initiatives while bringing organization and discipline to execution.

Employee Value Proposition

This opportunity is for a leader who wants to influence both a brand’s voice and how an organization communicates. You will have room to improve processes, develop talent, and build a communications approach that grows with the business.

Plexus offers a fast-paced environment that challenges, mentors, and rewards strong performance through financial recognition and career opportunities. Your work will directly influence the Ambassador and customer experience while helping employees connect to our mission, values, and priorities.

Key Performance Objectives

• Build a unified communications strategy. Align internal and external communications around audience needs and business priorities, with clear goals, channel plans, and ownership that support engagement, recruiting, and retention.

• Strengthen and protect the Plexus voice. Establish practical voice and tone standards that bring consistency to messaging while adapting appropriately to different audiences, markets, and channels.

• Improve communication planning and execution. Implement processes that clarify priorities, streamline approvals, manage competing requests, and help the team deliver accurate, compelling communications on time.

• Demonstrate and improve results. Establish performance measures and use data and audience feedback to improve message relevance, campaign effectiveness, and the Ambassador, customer, and employee experience.

Performance Accountabilities

Lead communications strategy and brand voice

• Set the vision, strategy, and goals for the communications team, connecting daily execution to company priorities.

• Guide messaging, copywriting, and editing to ensure communications consistently reflect the Plexus brand.

• Translate complex or sensitive information into clear, audience-appropriate messages.

Partner with Sales and Marketing to support growth

• Develop coordinated communications plans for product launches, incentives, promotions, international initiatives, and events.

• Build strong cross-functional relationships that align stakeholders on priorities, timing, and messaging.

• Deliver relevant communications across channels that help Ambassadors grow their businesses and strengthen customer engagement and retention.

Strengthen internal communications

• Guide employee communications that bring the company’s mission, vision, and values to life.

• Help employees understand products, initiatives, and business priorities through timely, meaningful messaging.

Build team capability and operational discipline

• Establish clear roles, expectations, workflows, and accountability.

• Hire, coach, and develop team members while removing barriers to effective execution.

• Manage vendor relationships and deliverables to support quality and departmental goals.

• Monitor results, report progress, and recommend creative, practical improvements grounded in data and feedback.

Performance Qualifications

• Communications leadership: Eight years leading communications and/or marketing teams, including at least three years as a manager.

• Exceptional writing and editing: Demonstrated ability to create compelling copy, develop a distinctive brand voice, and coach others to apply it consistently.

• Strategic planning and execution: Experience turning business objectives into coordinated communications plans with measurable results.

• Collaboration and influence: Ability to build productive relationships across functions, manage competing interests, and gain alignment.

• Organization and adaptability: Strong planning skills, attention to detail, and the ability to anticipate obstacles and adjust to changing priorities.

• People leadership: Experience hiring, developing, and motivating teams while establishing clear expectations and accountability.

• Judgment and discretion: Ability to communicate difficult, sensitive, and confidential information with tact.

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in communications, marketing, journalism, business, or equivalent related experience.

• Work environment: Plexus is onsite 5 days a week.

About Plexus

Founded in gut health. Experts in microbiome. Plexus Worldwide®, headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, is a renowned direct-selling company recognized as a top employer. Over the past 18 years, Plexus has dedicated itself to promoting hope, health, and happiness through its scientifically backed, innovative dietary supplements, weight management products, and personal care products, sold primarily through Plexus Brand Ambassadors. As a six-time Best Places to Work awardee, Blue Zone-approved employer, and an AZ Most Admired Company, Plexus prides itself on its robust organizational culture and commitment to community support and philanthropy. Our team is driven by a shared mission to empower individuals to achieve their health and wellness goals while offering additional income through the sale of products. Join us to be part of a team that values people, innovation, wellness, and community impact.

Benefits

• Highly rated and competitive medical plans.

• 401 (k) with company match and immediate vesting.

• 1-on-1, personalized health coaching.

• Many other voluntary benefits.

To learn more about Plexus Worldwide, please review our careers page at www.plexusworldwide.com/careers.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer

We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer.  This is a mid-level engineer position who independently designs, builds, tests, and maintains cloud-native and AI-native software components with limited supervision. The IC3 engineer takes ownership of medium-complexity features or components, works across the full development lifecycle from design through production support, and begins to mentor junior engineers. They combine solid software engineering fundamentals with growing expertise in AI/ML integration, ServiceNow platform development, and production systems. This role requires the ability to balance technical depth with broader team needs, communicate clearly with teammates and customers, and take initiative in improving code quality and product reliability.

What you get to do in this role:

Responsibility Area: Software Development & Feature Ownership

•    Design, develop, test, and maintain AI-native software features and backend services with limited supervision

•    Take full ownership of medium-complexity features from design through deployment and production support

•    Contribute to technical specifications, implementation plans, prompt design, agent logic, and retrieval workflows

•    Build comprehensive unit tests, integration tests, and basic evaluation checks for AI features

•    Troubleshoot software defects, integration issues, and AI behavior problems in development and production environments

•    Follow secure coding practices, including responsible handling of prompts, customer data, privacy, and AI safety guardrails

•    Work with cloud services, APIs, containers, and CI/CD pipelines to support reliable delivery of software

•    Proactively identify and fix technical debt in code you maintain; suggest improvements to teammates

Responsibility Area: ServiceNow Platform Development

•    Design and develop features and customizations on the ServiceNow platform independently

•    Architect ServiceNow workflows, business rules, and automations; implement client and server-side JavaScript/GlideScript

•    Design data models, forms, dashboards, and reports for ServiceNow applications; optimize database queries

•    Integrate third-party AI/ML services and custom APIs with ServiceNow; build REST integrations and webhooks

•    Maintain and extend ServiceNow plugins and apps; follow platform best practices and architectural patterns

•    Participate in ServiceNow platform upgrades and manage feature compatibility with platform updates

•    Support customer implementations and provide guidance on ServiceNow platform capabilities and configuration

Responsibility Area: Communication & Collaboration

•    Communicate clearly with team members, stakeholders, and cross-functional partners on technical topics

•    Provide regular updates on assigned work, risks, blockers, and delivery progress

•    Explain technical choices, implementation trade-offs, and AI limitations to technical and non-technical audiences

•    Participate actively in design discussions, code reviews, sprint planning, and retrospectives

•    Share knowledge with junior engineers through pair programming, code reviews, and informal mentoring

•    Work collaboratively with product, design, and other engineering teams; seek alignment on requirements

•    Communicate proactively about challenges and escalate issues appropriately

Responsibility Area: Technical Ownership & Quality

•    Own medium-complexity features or components from design through delivery and production support

•    Review code from peers and provide practical feedback on maintainability, correctness, and test coverage

•    Support root cause analysis for customer-reported issues, including defects involving retrieval quality or model output behavior

•    Mentor junior engineers informally by sharing implementation guidance, debugging approaches, and good engineering practices

•    Participate in on-call support for assigned components; respond to production issues and customer escalations

•    Drive improvements to development tools, testing infrastructure, and deployment processes in your areas

•    Learn from production incidents and help establish practices to prevent recurrence

Responsibility Area: Customer Support & Success

•    Engage with customers to understand and resolve complex technical issues

•    Participate in customer issue triage, investigation, and root cause analysis

•    Provide technical guidance to customers on application usage, configuration, and troubleshooting

•    Contribute to customer documentation, knowledge bases, and internal runbooks

•    Support critical customer escalations; own investigation and resolution of assigned issues

•    Gather customer feedback and communicate product improvement opportunities to product management

•    Help identify patterns in customer issues that could prevent future problems

To be successful in this role you have:

• 6+ years of software development experience with a Bachelor's degree; OR 3+ years with a Master's degree; OR a PhD without experience; OR equivalent work experience.
• 1+ years of hands-on experience with LLM prompt engineering, AI/ML API integration, or similar AI-native development
• 1+ years of hands-on experience developing applications or customizations on the ServiceNow platform
• Strong proficiency in Python, Java, or JavaScript; growing proficiency across multiple languages
• Solid understanding of JavaScript/GlideScript and ServiceNow platform APIs and data models
• Experience with cloud platforms (AWS/GCP/Azure) and basic familiarity with managed AI services
• Solid understanding of relational and NoSQL databases; familiarity with vector databases is a plus
• Experience with RESTful APIs, microservices architecture, and modern backend frameworks
• Understanding of software testing practices; ability to write effective unit and integration tests
• Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and automated testing frameworks
• Experience with version control systems and collaborative development workflows
• Strong problem-solving skills and ability to debug complex issues
• Good communication skills; ability to explain technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences
• Experience with Agile and Scrum development methodologies
• Demonstrated ability to take ownership of features and deliver them successfully
• Experience working with customers or in support-facing roles is a plus
• Familiarity with LLM orchestration frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex) or vector databases is a plus
• Understanding of AI/ML evaluation practices and responsible AI principles
